label: t3-lumen-law
topic: Track 3 (lumen geometry) mapped against law set 1.8.1, with one new checked Lean law
summary: Against law set 1.8.1 only physiology-laplace (accepted, Delphi.Physiology.laplace_pressure_limit) is a lumen-mechanics law; perturb-pressure, the scaling laws, turing-ddi and fisher-kpp-speed bear weakly. The Plateau, hexagon, Murray and Thompson-cell modules cited by the older map exist only in the upstream 1.6.0 tree and are absent from the application repo, whose own failed-theorem records say they were never compiled. New easy law lumen-area-ceiling (apical-length ceiling on normalised lumen area) written in LumenAreaCeiling.lean: first check FAILED (one linarith error, sorryAx in 3 theorems); after one fix check.sh reported errors=0, sorryAx=0, ALL CHECKED. The planar isoperimetric inequality is a named hypothesis, not proved.
lay_summary: We checked which proven rules in our library say anything about the hollow inside a ball of cells, like the air space in a tiny water balloon. Only one does: how much pressure a thin wall can hold before it tears. Some rules the earlier survey counted are not in the current library at all. So we wrote one new rule and had the proof checker confirm it. It says that if you know how many cells ring the hollow and how long each cell's inner edge is, the hollow's area cannot exceed a fixed limit, like a fixed length of fence that can only enclose so much ground. Our first proof attempt failed; the second passed.

area_ceiling: 0<AL, 0<p, 0<N, 0<A0, ipq AL p <= 1 implies normArea AL A0 <= ceiling N (apicalLen p N A0), with ipq A p = 4*pi*A/p^2, normArea = AL/A0, apicalLen = p/(N*sqrt A0), ceiling N la = (N*la)^2/(4*pi). Passes check.sh. The isoperimetric inequality is a named hypothesis hIPQ, not proved.
key_claims.evidence_quote: ALL CHECKED: no errors, no sorryAx

could_not_find: No external citations fetched this run; Vasquez et al. 2021 (doi 10.1038/s41467-021-25050-3) is only referenced via design-lumen.json and not re-verified here, so not listed as verified.
Data-map definitions (la = p/(N sqrt A0), a = AL/A0, IPQ = 4 pi AL/p^2) are transcribed from design-lumen.json, not re-read from the paper.
The planar isoperimetric inequality is assumed (hypothesis hIPQ), not derived in Lean.
check.sh output hides per-theorem axiom lists on success; I saw only the count of zero sorryAx and 6/6 axiom lines. Axiom lists were visible only on the failed first run.
I did not run lake build on the application repo or Audit.lean, and did not re-run the upstream cell-geometry modules.
The ceiling is circular as a test of a lumen's own la (ipq_identity shows this); its use is as a data-quality and design-space bound, not a held-out prediction.
